note:
LIED — Vienna 1814. Schubert, seventeen years old, sets Goethe's
"Gretchen am Spinnrade" on the 19th of October 1814 — the dated
autograph survives — and the German art song arrives whole: the
piano is the spinning wheel, not an accompaniment, and the song
is through-composed against the strophic poem. Fills a decade the
catalog jumped (nothing between Vienna 1785 and Boston 1831), and
it is the missing step in the salon lineage this table already
carries — `nocturne` (Paris 1835) is this music with the voice
folded into the right hand.
THE AXES: CAST is the whole claim — TWO equal players, the voice
and the piano figure, and the figure never stops (Gretchen's
wheel turns for the entire song). Development is the figure's
constancy against the voice's escalation.

LINEAGE: `classical` (Vienna 1785) is the harmonic language and
the city; `ballad` (London 1666) is the strophic narrative song
the lied is the art-music answer to — Schubert's own ballads
(Erlkönig, a year later) descend from Zumsteeg's, which descend
from exactly this stock.

WHO SINGS: confessional — the intimate, close voice; a
lied is sung to a room, not a hall, and the modern
singer-songwriter mouth is its direct heir.

CLOSEST, ANSWERED 2026-09-03 (the catalogue round, shift 3). The QA report's
`closest` column ranks each declared parent against every older row by a FEATURE
VECTOR — bpm, swing, major/minor, kit density, harmony kind, plan, nobass,
instrumental, family — and calls a parent sitting in the further half of that
ranking suspect. The vector has no term for the thing a child actually TAKES
from a parent, so an ancestor the record deliberately departs from ranks far by
construction, and the catalogue's trunk rows — funk, jazz, swing, ballad,
ambient, punk, drone, gregorian — rank far from nearly every leaf they grew.
THE PARENTS ON THIS ROW STAND. What the vector cannot see: `ballad` is called far and it is the FORM: a strophic song for one voice with a
story in it, which is what Schubert set. The vector scores an unaccompanied 1666
singer against an 1815 voice-and-piano on kit density and plan, and hears a piano
as a distance. `concerto` (1725) is offered as nearer on a shared arc.

THE DYNAMIC FIGURE (2026-09-06, the dynamics flood, shift 1): `dyn:
"arch"` — the line arches up and back down. One voice shaping one line:
up to the middle and back. The `roots` cluster takes `lean`; the
anchor's own evidence outranks it, which is the flood's rule
(docs/DYNAMICS-FLOOD.md).
